results.title: How to compare GPU cloud prices without fooling yourself - DEV Community
results.author: Runcrate
highlights:
"H100 from $X an hour" is the least useful number in a GPU price list. Two offers with the same headline can differ by a factor of two in what you pay at the end of the month, and two offers with very different headlines can come out the same.

...

It works for any provider, ours included. I'll use our public pricing endpoint for the examples because it's the data I can show you with a script, not because the method depends on it.

## 1. Get to one unit: dollars per GPU-hour 

Some lists quote the machine, some quote the GPU. An 8x H100 node at a per-machine price looks eight times worse than a 1x H100 at a per-GPU price. Divide by the GPU count first, always.

Runcrate's endpoint already reports per GPU-hour and needs no API key: 

```
import requests

data = requests.get("https://www.runcrate.ai/api/gpu-pricing").json()
print("fetched at", data["fetched_at"])

for g in data["gpus"]:
    s = g["specs"]
    per_gpu = s["num_gpus"] or 1
    print(
        f'{g["name"]:12} {g["vram"]:>6}  '
        f'${g["min_price_hr"]:.2f} to ${g["max_price_hr"]:.2f} per GPU-hr  '
        f'{g["available_options"]:>2} configs  GPUs per machine {g["gpu_counts"]}  '
        f'~{s["vcpus"] // per_gpu} vCPU / {s["memory_gb"] // per_gpu} GB RAM per GPU'
    )

```

Part of what it printed when I ran it (fetched at 2026-10-21T00:51 UTC): 

```
H100 SXM       80GB  $3.38 to $7.79 per GPU-hr   7 configs  GPUs per machine [1, 8]  ~20 vCPU / 128 GB RAM per GPU
A100 80GB      80GB  $1.76 to $4.26 per GPU-hr  12 configs  GPUs per machine [1, 2, 8]  ~28 vCPU / 120 GB RAM per GPU
L40S           48GB  $1.14 to $1.95 per GPU-hr  10 configs  GPUs per machine [1, 2, 4, 8]  ~12 vCPU / 72 GB RAM per GPU
A6000          48GB  $0.65 to $2.51 per GPU-hr  18 configs  GPUs per machine [1, 2, 4]  ~28 vCPU / 58 GB RAM per GPU

```

Notice the ranges. One GPU model can have a dozen configurations with a 2x to 4x spread between them. A comparison that keeps only the minimum hides that the minimum might be one 8-GPU node in one region.

## 2. Compare the same GPU, not the same name 

"A100" is two products (40 GB and 80 GB). "H100" is SXM or PCIe, with different memory bandwidth and interconnect. A "4090" with 24 GB will not hold the model your 48 GB card holds. Before comparing prices, match:

- VRAM (the endpoint has `vram` per GPU type)
- form factor and interconnect for multi-GPU work (`interconnect`, for example NVLink)
- GPU count per machine, because you can't split an 8-GPU node

If your model needs 80 GB, the price of a 40 GB card is irrelevant, however low it is.

...

## 6. Date every number 

GPU prices change weekly, sometimes daily. A comparison without a date is a guess. Put the fetch time next to every price (the endpoint returns `fetched_at` for that reason), and re-run your script rather than reusing last month's table.

...

Written with AI assistance. The script and prices above were run against the live endpoint on 2026-10-21.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

highlights:
What changed, read on verda.com/pricing on Nov 4, 2026 (unrounded page figures in brackets): GB300 $13.18 → $13.31 [$13.31], B300 $11.46 → $11.57 [$11.57], B200 $8.96 → $9.05 [$9.048], H200 $6.31 → $6.38 [$6.376], H100 SXM $4.84 → $4.89 [$4.889], A100 80GB $2.27 → $2.29 [$2.293], A100 40GB $1.63 → $1.64 [$1.641], RTX PRO 6000 $2.67 → $2.70 [$2.698] and L40S $1.92 → $1.94 [$1.939]. Each move is within a whisker of +1.0% — a uniform list adjustment, not one card repricing.

...

What it costs: Verda holds the board's Best offer on only two cards — the GB300 and the A100 40GB — and both rose today, so those two best offers rose with it. Everywhere else the cheapest verified offers are other providers' and none moved: the board's H100 SXM best is still TensorDock at $2.25 an hour (at an 8-GPU minimum) and its B200 best is still RunPod Community at $5.98. If you rent at Verda around the clock, today's rise adds about $95 a month per GB300, $66 per B200 and $37 per H100 on a 730-hour month — small per hour, real per fleet.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

results.title: GPU Market Report: 2026-11-06 — overfeed.news
results.author: overfeed.news editorial desk
highlights:
The RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q price on vast.ai rose 60.4 percent yesterday to $2.3578 per hour, marking the largest single-day increase among tracked GPUs, while the RTX 4090D price fell 48.4 percent to $6.6622 per hour.

## Daily Price Movements

Ten GPU models changed price by more than 1 percent compared to 2026-11-05. The RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q, with 96 GB of VRAM, increased from $1.4704 to $2.3578 per hour. The RTX 2060S, with 8 GB of VRAM, increased from $0.0662 to $0.1084 per hour, a 63.7 percent rise. The A100 SXM4, with 80 GB of VRAM, increased from $0.6006 to $0.8447 per hour, and the A100 PCIE, with 40 GB of VRAM, increased from $0.5356 to $0.7344 per hour.

Conversely, the RTX 4090D, with 48 GB of VRAM, decreased from $12.923 to $6.6622 per hour. The RTX PRO 4500, with 32 GB of VRAM, decreased from $0.72 to $0.4016 per hour. The H200 NVL, with 140 GB of VRAM, decreased from $3.79 to $2.6681 per hour. The RTX 3070 Ti and RTX 4060, both with 8 GB of VRAM, decreased by 33.5 percent and 30.5 percent respectively. The GTX 1660 Ti, with 6 GB of VRAM, increased by 35.5 percent to $0.0859 per hour. Fifty-three chips remained unchanged or moved within 1 percent.

results.title: Cloud GPU Prices per Hour 2026, in Crypto | GPUwithCrypto
highlights:
# GPUwithCrypto prices 2026: how much does a cloud GPU cost per hour?

Last updated: November 13, 2026 · 13 min read

How much does a GPU cost per hour at GPUwithCrypto?

An H100 80GB costs $2.32/hour at GPUwithCrypto, an A100 80GB $0.92/hour and an RTX 4090 $0.28/hour, billed per minute and paid in crypto with no KYC. On 13 November 2026, these prices were below the mean on-demand price of 5 rivals on 7 of 7 GPUs; marketplace and community offers were lower on 5.

In brief

- Seven GPUs, one price each per GPU-hour: H100 $2.32, H200 $3.07, B200 $4.61, A100 80GB $0.92, L40S $0.82, RTX 4090 $0.28, RTX 5090 $0.42.
- Sold as blocks of GPU-hours (10, 24, 168 or 720 hours of one GPU model), used per minute while an instance runs; unused hours do not expire.
- Paid in crypto only (BTC, USDT, USDC, ETH, SOL, LTC, XMR) from a prepaid balance, minimum top-up $25; the sending wallet pays the network fee and GPUwithCrypto adds none.
- Against on-demand list prices (13 November 2026): from −20% (L40S) to −58% (RTX 4090) under the mean of Massed Compute, Thunder Compute, RunPod, Lambda and Salad.
- Where rivals are cheaper: a community, interruptible or marketplace offer was below GPUwithCrypto on the H100, A100 80GB, L40S, RTX 4090 and RTX 5090.
- No KYC: no ID, no card, an account number as login; GPUs are prepared by hand by the team and billing starts only when the GPU runs.

...

- One price per provider, GPU and offer type. When a provider lists several configurations for the same GPU, the lowest listed price was kept, and the listing is recorded in the data.

- The median of an even number of prices is the mean of the two middle values.
